paragraphs: On Thursday evening, the phone rang in Lily's house. Mom was in the kitchen, and Tom was in his room. Lily picked up the phone and said, "Hello, this is Lily." "Hello, my dear," said the person on the phone. "This is Grandma." "Hello, Grandma!" said Lily. "Is everything fine?" "Yes, I am calling about Saturday," said Grandma. "Your dad is driving to Green Hill, but the old bridge is closed."

"Please take a pencil and write the directions," said Grandma. Lily took a pencil and a sheet of paper. She wrote every word, because she wanted no mistakes. "First, drive along the big road for ten minutes," said Grandma. "Then turn left at the big blue sign." "Go straight until you see a small shop." "Our house is the third house after the shop, and it has a green gate." Lily repeated the directions, and Grandma said, "That is right." "Don't turn right at the river," said Grandma, "because that road goes to the old bridge."

"The weather will be bad on Saturday," said Grandma. "It will rain all morning." "However, don't worry, because I have a surprise for you." "What is it?" asked Lily. "It is a white raincoat with a red stripe on each arm," said Grandma. "Oh, thank you!" said Lily. "I have a blue one for Tom," said Grandma, "because he likes simple things." Lily laughed, because Grandma knew Tom very well.

"Grandma, can I ask a question for the blog?" asked Lily. "Of course," said Grandma. "How long have you and Grandpa been married?" "We have been married for forty-two years," said Grandma. "Wow, that is a long time!" said Lily. "What is the secret?" "Grandpa says, 'The secret is to listen,'" said Grandma. "You are a very good grandchild, because you always listen."

Then Grandma said, "Grandpa is here, and he says, 'Bring Pip.'" "We will," said Lily. "See you on Saturday, Grandma!" When Dad came home, Lily gave him the paper with the directions. He read it twice and said, "This is perfect." Lily smiled, because she liked her new job as the family map.
text.summary: Grandma phones Lily and gives the directions to her house in Green Hill. She tells Lily about a surprise raincoat, and Lily asks her a question for the blog.

sentences.text: On Thursday evening, the phone rang in Lily's house.
Mom was in the kitchen, and Tom was in his room.
Lily picked up the phone and said, "Hello, this is Lily."
"Hello, my dear," said the person on the phone.
"This is Grandma."
"Hello, Grandma!" said Lily.
"Is everything fine?"
"Yes, I am calling about Saturday," said Grandma.
"Your dad is driving to Green Hill, but the old bridge is closed."
"Please take a pencil and write the directions," said Grandma.
Lily took a pencil and a sheet of paper.
She wrote every word, because she wanted no mistakes.
"First, drive along the big road for ten minutes," said Grandma.
"Then turn left at the big blue sign."
"Go straight until you see a small shop."
"Our house is the third house after the shop, and it has a green gate."
Lily repeated the directions, and Grandma said, "That is right."
"Don't turn right at the river," said Grandma, "because that road goes to the old bridge."
"The weather will be bad on Saturday," said Grandma.
"It will rain all morning."
"However, don't worry, because I have a surprise for you."
"What is it?" asked Lily.
"It is a white raincoat with a red stripe on each arm," said Grandma.
"Oh, thank you!" said Lily.
"I have a blue one for Tom," said Grandma, "because he likes simple things."
Lily laughed, because Grandma knew Tom very well.
"Grandma, can I ask a question for the blog?" asked Lily.
"Of course," said Grandma.
"How long have you and Grandpa been married?"
"We have been married for forty-two years," said Grandma.
"Wow, that is a long time!" said Lily.
"What is the secret?"
"Grandpa says, 'The secret is to listen,'" said Grandma.
"You are a very good grandchild, because you always listen."
Then Grandma said, "Grandpa is here, and he says, 'Bring Pip.'"
"We will," said Lily.
"See you on Saturday, Grandma!"
When Dad came home, Lily gave him the paper with the directions.
He read it twice and said, "This is perfect."
Lily smiled, because she liked her new job as the family map.
